harry: quick proposal: introduce a tiny runtime-side "iidx" (index-of-indices) that the transport can assemble on read when a canonical manifest/sidx is missing. goal: let the runtime stitch checkpoints on-demand for composed objects and support progressive verification without blocking the warmup path.

nina: "index-of-indices"? can you sketch what it contains and who builds it?

harry: sure. iidx is produced by transport-side logic (or a separate indexer service) at read-time. shape: ordered list of (object_id, range_start, range_end, chunk_id_hint, checksum_hint). it purposely keeps entries coarse-grained (e.g., 4MB blocks) to avoid pathological metadata blowup. example snippet: ```
[
  {obj: "o-123", start:0, end:4194304, hint: "layer-0", chk: "sha1:..."},
  {obj: "o-124", start:0, end:2097152, hint: "layer-2", chk: null}
]
```

oliver: how is this different from sidx? seems similar.

harry: iidx is intentionally ephemeral and coarse. sidx is an ingest-time, authoritative index aligned to model layer boundaries. iidx is a pragmatic fallback for: (a) composed/tar uploads where no single sidx exists, (b) cases where we want to avoid re-ingest for minor reshards, (c) cross-variant stitch where uploader didn't emit variant-specific sidx. it lets the runtime proceed with a best-effort plan.

mike: verification: we can't accept unsigned guesses. what's the strategy to avoid silent corruption?

harry: two layers: first, iidx carries checksum_hints when available; second, verification is offloaded to a verifier-worker pool that runs asynchronously and can mark ranges as "verified" or "suspect". runtime can start streaming unverified ranges in read-only "optimistic" mode but gate GPU-facing activations until critical layers are verified or fallback thresholds hit. if verifier reports mismatch, runtime evicts affected ranges and triggers fallback fetch or recompose.

nina: optimistic streaming + async verify is scary but could yield big cold-start wins. how to limit IO blowup? many small reads would hurt.

harry: iidx entries include a coalesce_hint and a preferred_fetch (http-range or direct-mmap). runtime's prefetcher implements a lookahead window and coalesces adjacent iidx entries into larger range reads. also we add a budget token to limit outstanding range requests per runtime instance.

oliver: compatibility with legacy loaders?

harry: provide stream-proxy shim that implements the legacy chunk-iterator API by reading iidx + issuing ranged reads. new loaders can request iidx directly (via transport query param ?index=best-effort). migration is opt-in.

mike: ops playbook? what if verifier pool falls behind and many runtimes are in optimistic mode?

harry: we'll expose circuit-breaker metrics: iidx_pending_verifies, iidx_verify_latency, optimistic_ratio. If pending verifies > X or verify_latency > Y, runtime auto-throttles to manifest-only path and signals upgrade_required. ops-bot: annotate: if "iidx circuit" trips, auto-disable iidx for that namespace and send alert.

ops-bot: alert rule created: iidx_verify_latency > 10s for > 5m -> p1 alert to infra-oncall. :robot_face:

nina: testing: we need a harness that composes tarball-of-shards artifacts and exercises off-by-one and partial-object semantics. also test variant mismatch (q4_0 vs fp16) and verify that optimistic streaming never exposes bad activations to GPU.

harry: agreed. test-suite: (1) synthetic composer that builds multi-object checkpoint, (2) fuzz ranges with partial writes, (3) slow verifier to simulate backlog, (4) damage-injection that flips a checksum and ensures eviction/fallback.

oliver: telemetry? we need to measure cold-start delta and the fraction of runs that completed without fallback.

harry: telemetry fields: iidx_used (bool), iidx_verify_time(ms), optimistic_first_layer_ready(ms), iidx_evictions, iidx_fallbacks, iidx_coalesce_efficiency. also correlated hotstart-trace with timeline events: index_assembled, first_prefetch, first_layer_ready, verifier_ok.

mike: performance concerns: verifier pool CPU + network. do we want verifier to be colocated or shared?

harry: prefer small verifier fleet colocated near transport nodes to minimize egress; can autoscale via queue depth. we should measure cost vs benefit. also allow config: verify_policy = {eager, async, none} per-namespace. default: async for canary namespaces.

nina: rollout: 1) implement iidx assembler & stream-proxy in transport, internal canary on a few non-critical models; 2) run fuzz + load test; 3) enable optimistic mode for canary; 4) gather telemetry for 2 weeks; 5) expand opt-in. default-off for Dedicated/Private.

harry: I'll draft the follow-up RFC with interfaces (transport query, iidx shape, verifier protocol), the test harness, and an ops runbook. posting by EOD. thanks for the quick review. :thumbsup:
